**No president signed an "Antarctic Statehood Act". The question rests on a false premise.** I found no evidence that such a law or bill exists, or that Antarctica is a U.S. state. The count of U.S. states is still 50.

I used 3 of the 8 retrievals: 1 search and 2 page reads.

**Claims**

- A web search for "Antarctic Statehood Act Antarctica 51st state" returned no bill or law with that name. The results included only unrelated Antarctic laws, a speculative Quora thread, and Greenland statehood coverage.
  - https://www.quora.com/If-Antarctica-became-the-51st-state-what-would-it-mean-for-each-of-the-research-stations-on-the-continent
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_state
- The closest real item is a House bill to make Greenland the 51st state, introduced by Rep. Randy Fine. It is a proposal, not a law, and it concerns Greenland, not Antarctica.
  - https://thehill.com/homenews/house/5685118-fine-introduces-greenland-bill/
  - https://www.newsweek.com/greenland-could-become-51st-state-under-proposed-bill-11349217
- The Wikipedia page on the "51st state" discusses Puerto Rico and other candidates. The text I read did not mention Antarctica.
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_state
- The Antarctic Treaty, signed in 1959, prohibits "the making of new territorial claims in Antarctica." That is a legal obstacle to any state claiming the continent. The same page says the U.S. made no territorial claim there.
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antarctic_Treaty_System

**Limits of this evidence**

- Wikipedia is the only source for the treaty claims, and I did not corroborate them elsewhere.
- I did not search the official Congress.gov record. My conclusion is based on absence, so it is not proof that no such bill was ever introduced.
- The Greenland-bill details come from the search-result summaries. I did not open those articles.
